mainTopic: How the פסוקים and stories prove that a husband inherits his wife (בעל יורש את אשתו), and the debate over whether land 'already transferred' still counts as moving between tribes.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא from the previous daf that proves a husband inherits his wife (בעל יורש את אשתו). The ברייתא ends with יאיר, who owned cities his father שגוב never had. The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs so many פסוקים, each introduced with 'ואומר'. It explains that each פסוק from במדבר could be pushed off: maybe it is about the son, or maybe it only adds a לאו. That is why the ברייתא turns to the stories of אלעזר and פנחס and of יאיר. Two such stories cannot both be about a son, so together they prove the point. רב פפא challenges this to אביי: maybe פנחס and יאיר bought their land or got it as a שדה חרמים. אביי answers from the פסוק itself: the 'son' reading still lets the mother's land leave her tribe, and we do not say 'already transferred'. Finally רב יימר asks רב אשי how marrying within the father's tribe could ever help without that idea. רב אשי answers that she marries a man whose father and mother match her own parents' tribes.

steps.title: Yair's cities came from his wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the case of יאיר. He had cities his father שגוב never had, so he must have inherited them from his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did יאיר have land that his father שגוב did not have? It teaches that יאיר married a woman, she died, and he inherited from her.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that started on the previous daf. Its last proof that a husband inherits his wife is the story of יאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יאיר had 23 cities, but his father שגוב had none, so יאיר could not have gotten them from his father. The only explanation left is that his wife inherited land, she died, and יאיר inherited it from her. That shows a husband inherits his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of שגוב, who owned 23 cities in the land of גלעד
Father of יאיר, who did not own those cities
'It teaches': it shows us a lesson
'And he inherited her': he inherited her property
A husband inherits his wife's property

phrases.english: And from where did Yair have [land]
phrases.notes: This goes back to the פסוק in דברי הימים א 2:22 that says יאיר had 23 cities.

phrases.english: that Seguv did not have?
This teaches that Yair married a woman
and she died, and he inherited her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִנַּיִן לְיָאִיר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לִשְׂגוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of proofs in the ברייתא that began on the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: A husband inherits his wife's property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק that יאיר owned 23 cities that his father שגוב did not own.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא keep saying 'and it says'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to add more and more פסוקים with 'ואומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא brings extra פסוקים when the first one already seemed to prove the point. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'ואומר' adds another proof, which suggests the earlier proof was not airtight. The גמרא wants to know what weakness each new פסוק is fixing. The next steps answer this one פסוק at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What?': what does it mean or why is it needed
'And it says': brings an additional פסוק as further proof
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

phrases.english: What is [the point of] "and it says"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְאוֹמֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing how it is built.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא needs several פסוקים instead of just the first one.

steps.title: Maybe the first verse is only worried about the son
steps.stepSummary: Someone could push off the first פסוק. Maybe it only worries that the land will pass to another tribe through the son, and a husband does not inherit at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the פסוק is worried about land moving through the son, but a husband does not inherit...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It shows how someone could brush aside the first פסוק, which told a daughter who inherits to marry within her father's tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (במדבר 36:8) only says the heiress should marry within her tribe. That rule could be explained by the son: he belongs to his father's tribe, so when he inherits his mother the land leaves her tribe. If so, the פסוק proves nothing about a husband inheriting.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': introduces a possible objection
A transfer of land caused by the son inheriting
'The פסוק is concerned about'
'A husband does not inherit'

phrases.english: And if you will say,
the verse is concerned about a transfer through the son,
phrases.notes: The son belongs to his father's tribe, so if he inherits his mother, her land moves to his tribe.

phrases.english: but a husband does not inherit –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, בְּסִבַּת הַבֵּן קָא קָפֵיד קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 2 by showing that the first פסוק could be pushed off.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the first פסוק as a proof that a husband inherits.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule could be explained entirely by the son inheriting, so the husband does not have to be involved.

steps.title: Second verse: the land must not move between tribes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second פסוק, 'no inheritance shall move from tribe to tribe'. It seems extra, so it must teach that the husband himself inherits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And no inheritance of the children of Israel shall move from tribe to tribe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push-off with a second פסוק. This is why the ברייתא needed its first 'ואומר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about the son is already covered by the first פסוק, so this second פסוק looks extra. Its extra message is that land can also move to another tribe through the husband inheriting his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall move around': shall pass to someone else
Inheritance, here the family's land
From one tribe to another tribe

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"So no inheritance of the children of Israel shall move
from tribe to tribe."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״וְלֹא תִסֹּב נַחֲלָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמַּטֶּה לְמַטֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-off of step 3 with a second פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra פסוק in במדבר 36:7.

steps.title: Maybe the second verse only adds a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Someone could say the second פסוק is still about the son. It is only there to add a לאו on top of the עשה, so breaking the rule violates both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the second פסוק is there so that she violates a לאו and an עשה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the second proof. Maybe the extra פסוק has a different job and does not teach that a husband inherits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the second פסוק is not adding a new way for land to move. Instead it turns the same rule into a לאו, so the heiress who marries outside her tribe breaks both a לאו and an עשה. Then the husband is still not proven to inherit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To violate because of it': to break the rule
A negative commandment (a 'do not')
A positive commandment (a 'do')

phrases.english: And if you will say,
[it comes] to make one violate a prohibition and a positive command for it –
phrases.notes: The עשה is 'she shall be a wife to one of her father's tribe.' The לאו is 'no inheritance shall move.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, לַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו בְּלָאו וַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof of step 4 by giving the extra פסוק a different job.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the second פסוק as a proof that a husband inherits.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra פסוק could just be adding a לאו, not a new way for land to transfer.

steps.title: Third verse: from one tribe to another tribe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a third פסוק, 'no inheritance shall move from one tribe to another tribe', which again seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'No inheritance shall move from one tribe to another tribe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second push-off with yet another פסוק. This explains the ברייתא's next 'ואומר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו is already covered by the second פסוק, so this third פסוק seems extra again. Its extra job must be to teach that land moves through the husband inheriting his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Another tribe
A פסוק that seems extra, so it must teach something new
Transfer of land ownership

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"No inheritance shall move
from one tribe to another tribe."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״לֹא תִסֹּב נַחֲלָה מִמַּטֶּה לְמַטֶּה אַחֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-off of step 5 with a third פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra פסוק in במדבר 36:9.

steps.title: Maybe the third verse only adds a second prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Someone could say the third פסוק only adds a second לאו, so breaking the rule violates two לאוין and an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the third פסוק is there so that she violates two לאוין and an עשה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the third proof in the same way as before. Maybe the extra פסוק just adds another לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like step 5, the extra פסוק could be read as making the act more serious, not as a new source for a husband inheriting. The proofs from these פסוקים in במדבר therefore never fully close the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Two negative commandments
One who violates a commandment
An added prohibition

phrases.english: And if you will say,
[it comes] to make one violate two prohibitions and a positive command for it –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, לַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִין וַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof of step 6 the same way step 5 pushed off step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the third פסוק as a proof that a husband inherits.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra פסוק could just be adding a second לאו.

steps.title: Turning to the verse about אלעזר בן אהרן
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוקים in במדבר can all be pushed off, the גמרא turns to a story in יהושע about אלעזר בן אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And אלעזר son of אהרן died...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the פסוקים of laws and turns to a historical פסוק as proof. This explains the ברייתא's next 'ואומר', and the גמרא will explain this proof next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument about extra פסוקים can always be pushed off by giving each פסוק another job. A story about who actually owned land is a different kind of proof. The rest of that פסוק, which the גמרא will use, mentions land belonging to פינחס.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול after אהרן, father of פינחס
'Etc.': the פסוק continues
Son of אלעזר, mentioned in the rest of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא brings many פסוקים for one point because each פסוק in במדבר can be pushed off. Maybe it is about the son, or maybe it only adds a לאו. So the ברייתא keeps going to stronger proofs from history: אלעזר and יאיר.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Elazar the son of Aaron died, etc."
phrases.notes: יהושע 24:33. The rest of the פסוק mentions the hill of פינחס his son, which the גמרא explains next.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״וְאֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן מֵת וְגוֹ׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the פסוקים in במדבר can all be pushed off, it switches to a historical פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 24:33, about אלעזר בן אהרן and the land of פינחס.

steps.title: Maybe פנחס inherited the land from his mother
steps.stepSummary: Someone could say the land came to פנחס from his mother, not from his wife. That would make the story about a son inheriting, not a husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: it was אלעזר who married a woman, and she died, and פנחס inherited from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way to push off the proof from אלעזר's burial in פנחס's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof was that פנחס owned land his father אלעזר did not own, so it must have come from פנחס's wife. But maybe the land came from פנחס's mother, אלעזר's wife. If so, פנחס got it as a son, and the story says nothing about a husband inheriting.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. This opens a possible objection.
Married a woman
He inherited from her

phrases.english: And if you would say,
it was Elazar who married a woman
and she died, and Pinchas inherited from her
phrases.notes: He means פנחס's own mother, so פנחס got the land as her son.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, אֶלְעָזָר הוּא דִּנְסֵיב אִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof from the פנחס story in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from פנחס's land.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The land could have come to פנחס from his mother, which would make it a son's inheritance.

steps.title: A new proof from יאיר son of שגוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second story, about יאיר, which cannot be explained as a son inheriting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And שגוב fathered יאיר, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: To answer the push-off about פנחס, the גמרא brings a different פסוק about יאיר and his father שגוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to say that יאיר had cities in the land of גלעד. The point is that יאיר had land that did not come from his father, so it must have come through his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of יאיר
Son of שגוב, who owned cities in גלעד

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Seguv fathered Yair, etc."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:22. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק: יאיר had twenty-three cities in גלעד.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וּשְׂגוּב הוֹלִיד אֶת יָאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-off in step 9 by bringing a new source.
steps.raayaObject: A husband inherits his wife's land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 2:22, about יאיר son of שגוב

steps.title: Maybe יאיר also inherited from his mother
steps.stepSummary: Someone could try the same push-off for יאיר: maybe he also inherited from his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: there too it is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the יאיר story can be pushed off the same way as the פנחס story. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as פנחס might have inherited from his mother, יאיר might have inherited from his mother. Then this story would also be about a son inheriting.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the יאיר case
It is also like this

phrases.english: And if you would say,
there too it is the same,
phrases.notes: Meaning יאיר also got the land from his mother, just like the suggestion about פנחס.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הָתָם נָמֵי הָכִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the step 9 push-off to the new proof from step 10.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יאיר might also have inherited as a son, from his mother.

steps.title: Two stories would not be needed to teach the same thing
steps.stepSummary: If both stories only taught that a son inherits from his mother, one story would be enough. So at least one of them must be teaching that a husband inherits.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need two פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the push-off. Two stories teaching the very same thing would be extra, so one of them must teach that a husband inherits his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is from extra text. If both פנחס and יאיר only inherited from their mothers, the second story adds nothing new. Since the פסוקים do not repeat for nothing, the two stories together prove that a husband inherits.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why do I need two פסוקים?

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that a husband inherits his wife rests on both stories together, פנחס and יאיר. Two stories cannot both be only about a son inheriting.

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need two verses?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the push-off in step 11 and completes the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With two separate stories, at least one must show that a husband inherits his wife.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe the husband does not inherit, and they bought the land
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי. Maybe a husband does not inherit at all. The פסוקים are about a son, and פנחס and יאיר simply bought their land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: How do you know? Maybe I can really tell you: a husband does not inherit. The פסוקים are about land passing through a son, as we explained. And יאיר bought his land, and פנחס also bought his land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the whole proof. He offers a different explanation for every source the גמרא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in במדבר can be read as being about a son, as already explained in steps 5 and 7. The stories of פנחס and יאיר only show that they had land their fathers did not have. Buying the land explains that just as well as inheriting it from a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Perhaps
A husband does not inherit
Land passing over through a son
He actually bought it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
From where do you know?
Perhaps I can really say to you:
a husband does not inherit;
and the verses are about the son, as we answered;
phrases.notes: This points back to the answers in steps 5 and 7: the extra פסוקים only add more לאוין about the son.

phrases.english: and Yair, he bought it;
and Pinchas too, he bought it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 12 by giving a new reason why פנחס and יאיר had land.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that a husband inherits his wife, from the stories of פנחס and יאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Owning extra land does not prove inheritance from a wife. They could have bought it.

steps.title: אביי: פנחס could not have bought the land
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a bought field returns to its owner in the יובל. Then the צדיק אלעזר would end up buried in someone else's land.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You cannot say פנחס bought it. If so, the field would go back to its owner in the יובל, and a צדיק would be buried in a grave that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב פפא's idea for פנחס. Bought land returns to its owner in the יובל, so it would not stay a proper burial place for אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יובל year a field that was bought goes back to its original family. If פנחס had only bought the field, אלעזר's grave would one day be in land that was not his. That cannot be what happened, so the land must have been inherited. Notice that אביי answers only about פנחס, not about יאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say
The fiftieth year, when bought fields go back to their original owners
A righteous man. Here it means אלעזר.
A grave that is not his

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the פנחס story as a proof that a husband inherits his wife, because buying the land is ruled out.
steps.confusionAlert: The צדיק buried here is אלעזר, the father, not פנחס. The grave was in פנחס's land.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב פפא.

phrases.english: that Pinchas bought it
you cannot say;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן, נִמְצֵאת שָׂדֶה חוֹזֶרֶת בַּיּוֹבֵל,
phrases.english: for if so, the field would turn out to return in the Jubilee,
and a righteous man would turn out to be buried
in a grave that is not his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פִּנְחָס דִּזְבַן מִיזְבָּן לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 13, but only about פנחס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out the alternative explanation by showing what it would lead to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פנחס may have bought the land, so the story proves nothing about a husband inheriting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bought land returns in the יובל, which would leave אלעזר buried in land not his own. So פנחס must have inherited the land.

steps.title: Maybe פנחס got the land as a dedicated field
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that פנחס, as a כהן, received the land as a שדה חרמים, which never returns in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say that the land came to him as a dedicated field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back again on אביי's last answer. He offers another way פנחס could have owned the land without inheriting it from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had said that bought land goes back in the יובל, so it can't be the source of פנחס's land. רב פפא answers that a field dedicated as חרמים goes to the כהנים permanently, and פנחס was a כהן. So the land never has to return, and there is still no proof that a husband inherits.

keyTerms.meaning: A field dedicated with the word 'חרם'; it is given to the כהנים
It fell to him, meaning it came into his possession
Rather, say: introduces a new suggestion

phrases.english: Rather, say
that it came to him from a dedicated field!
phrases.notes: פנחס was a כהן, and a field like this goes to the כהנים for good. It does not go back in the יובל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ מִשְּׂדֵה חֲרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's יובל argument by finding a way to own land that never returns.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim in step 14 that פנחס could not have owned the land through purchase.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שדה חרמים belongs to a כהן permanently. So פנחס's ownership does not prove that a husband inherits.

steps.title: אביי: in the end the land still leaves the mother's tribe
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that even if only a son inherits, the land still moves from the mother's tribe to the father's tribe. So the פסוק must be talking about a husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In the end, the inheritance is uprooted from the mother's tribe to the father's tribe!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי leaves the story of פנחס behind and argues from the פסוק itself. He shows that the 'son' reading doesn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells a woman who inherits to marry within her tribe, so land won't move between tribes. But if she inherited from her mother, who came from another tribe, then her son still belongs to his father's tribe. The land leaves the mother's tribe either way, so the concern must be about a husband inheriting.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, no matter what
The inheritance is uprooted, meaning it leaves the tribe
Tribe

phrases.english: Abaye said: In the end,
the inheritance is being uprooted
from the mother's tribe to the father's tribe!
phrases.notes: Picture a woman who inherited from her mother, who came from a different tribe. Her son belongs to his father's tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סוֹף סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of answering the שדה חרמים idea directly, אביי shows that the פסוקים cannot be about a son.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק: the son reading would make the תורה's command pointless.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים about tribes could be speaking only about a son inheriting.
steps.terutzMaskana: A son reading still lets land move between tribes, so the פסוקים must be about a husband.

steps.title: Maybe the land counts as already transferred
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the תורה isn't worried about the mother's land. It was already considered transferred when the mother married the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you know? Perhaps it is different there, because it was already transferred!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects אביי's argument from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says that when the mother married a man from another tribe, her land was already treated as moving out of her tribe. So the תורה doesn't care if it moves again through her daughter's son. That means the 'son' reading of the פסוק can still work.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?
It is different there
Because it was already transferred

phrases.english: And from where? Perhaps it is different there,
because it was already transferred!
phrases.notes: He means it was transferred back when the mother married into the father's tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי? וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, שֶׁכְּבָר הוּסַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's argument in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's proof that the son reading fails.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed the תורה worries about land that was already treated as transferred.

steps.title: אביי: we don't use 'already transferred'
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the 'already transferred' idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We do not say 'because it was already transferred.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his argument. He refuses to accept the reasoning of 'already transferred.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as the woman owns the land, it still belongs to someone from the first tribe. So it has not really been transferred yet. That means אביי's argument from step 16 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not say, meaning we do not use this reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: אביי holds that the פסוקים teach that a husband inherits. He does this by rejecting the idea of 'already transferred.'

phrases.english: He said to him: 'Because it was already transferred' — we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שֶׁכְּבָר הוּסַבָּה לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's rejection in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother's land counts as already moved to another tribe.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not use 'already transferred,' so the son reading still fails.

steps.title: רב יימר begins a challenge: 'already transferred' lets the פסוק fit both cases
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר tells רב אשי that if we accept 'already transferred,' the פסוק can be about either a son or a husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רב אשי: It works well if you say 'already transferred.' Then the פסוק can be explained as being about a transfer through the son or through the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר starts a new challenge. This line is only the first half: the 'it works well if' part. The other half will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we accept 'already transferred,' marrying within her father's tribe always works. Land from her father stays in the tribe, and land from her mother was already transferred. So the פסוק fits a son or a husband equally. The coming difficulty is what happens if we reject that reasoning, as אביי did.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say: the first half of a challenge
The פסוק can be explained as being about a certain case
A transfer through the son
A transfer through the husband

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of רב יימר's challenge. 'אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא' only sets up the case that works. The real difficulty comes in the next line.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said to Rav Ashi:
It works well if you say 'because it was already transferred,'
that is how the verse can be explained

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּסִבַּת הַבֵּן, בֵּין בְּסִבַּת הַבַּעַל.
phrases.english: either as a transfer through the son or as a transfer through the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the argument over 'already transferred' to set up a new difficulty for אביי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rejection of 'already transferred' in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First half only: with 'already transferred,' the פסוק works for both a son and a husband. This suggests that rejecting it will cause a problem.

steps.title: Without 'already transferred,' even marrying inside her father's tribe moves land
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר finishes his challenge. If we do not say the mother's land was 'already transferred,' then the תורה's command to marry within the father's tribe would not stop the land from moving. The mother's land would still leave the mother's tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say we do NOT use the idea of 'it was already transferred,' then what good does it do when she marries someone from her father's tribe? Her mother's land is still being pulled out of her mother's tribe and into her father's tribe!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר is finishing the challenge he started in step 19. He shows that if we reject 'already transferred,' the תורה's command to marry within the father's tribe does not actually keep land in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a daughter who inherited land from her mother, and her mother came from a different tribe than her father. If she marries a man from her father's tribe, the land she got from her mother ends up in the father's tribe. So without the 'already transferred' idea, the פסוק's command seems unable to prevent land moving between tribes.

keyTerms.meaning: It was transferred (the land was already counted as moved to another tribe)
Her father's tribe (words from the פסוק)
Is uprooted (pulled out of its place)
Inheritance, family land
The mother's tribe

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new speaker. It is still רב יימר talking to רב אשי, finishing the 'if you say' half of his argument from step 19.

phrases.english: But if you say
we do not say "it was already transferred"
when she gets married to one
of the family of her father's tribe
what of it?
But an inheritance is uprooted
from the mother's tribe to the father's tribe!
phrases.notes: He means the land she inherited from her mother, who came from a different tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא אָמְרִינַן שֶׁכְּבָר הוּסַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יימר's two-sided argument from step 19 by showing the problem with rejecting 'already transferred.'
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rejection of the 'already transferred' idea (step 18)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without 'already transferred,' the תורה's command to marry within the father's tribe would still move the mother's land into the father's tribe, so the command could not fully work.

steps.title: Marry her to a man who matches both her parents' tribes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the command can still work even without 'already transferred.' She marries a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe, so the land keeps the same status it had with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רב אשי answered:] It works when we marry her to a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רב יימר's challenge by describing a specific match that keeps all the land where it belongs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a woman with parents from two tribes holds land from both tribes. רב אשי's solution is a husband with the very same 'mix': his father from her father's tribe, his mother from her mother's tribe. That way nothing changes when the land passes to him, so we do not need the 'already transferred' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: We marry (her) off
A man (the husband)
His father
His mother / her mother (depending on the spot)

steps.whatToRemember: Even if we do not say the mother's land was 'already transferred,' the פסוק's command can still be kept: match her with a husband whose father's tribe and mother's tribe are exactly like hers.

phrases.english: Where we marry her to a man
phrases.notes: The words 'רב אשי said to him' are not printed here, but the גמרא means this as his answer.

phrases.english: whose father is from her father's tribe
and his mother is from her mother's tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמַנְסְבִינַן לַהּ לְגַבְרָא דַּאֲבוּהִי מִשִּׁבְטָא דַאֲבוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יימר's challenge in step 20 by giving a case where the command works without 'already transferred.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a specific case where the problem does not come up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'already transferred,' every marriage within the father's tribe would still move the mother's land.
steps.terutzMaskana: A husband whose father and mother match her father's and mother's tribes keeps all the land in the same status, so the command still works.
